name: Easy Slow Cooker Pork Chop Cassoulet with White Beans, Carrots, Celery & Crunchy Topping

instructions.primary_message: Wash, dry, peel, and trim carrots; slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick rounds. Wash, dry, trim, and slice celery crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces. Place both in a medium bowl.
Peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl with the veggies and set aside.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 pork chops, boneless
½ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the chops and sear until golden, about 2 minutes per side (the chops will not be cooked all the way through). Transfer to a clean plate. (Reserve skillet with cooking juices for later use.)
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans. Place in a 4-quart slow cooker insert along with tomato sauce, broth, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 (15 oz) can cannellini (white kidney) beans
1 (8 fl oz) can tomato sauce
1 cup chicken or vegetable broth
¼ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Return the skillet (with cooking juices) to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add carrot, celery, onion, and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat, add to the slow cooker with the bean mixture, then stir to combine the stew.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tsp extra virgin olive oil
1 tbsp minced garlic

instructions.primary_message: Add seared pork chops (and any accumulated juices) to the slow cooker, nestling the chops into the stew. Cover and cook until chops are tender, 8-9 hours on LOW or 4-5 hours on HIGH. Remove from heat.
Just before serving, place croutons in a resealable plastic bag and gently crush using a rolling pin or the bottom of a saucepan.
To serve, divide stew, crushed croutons, Parmesan, and chops between plates or bowls. Enjoy!
